---
title: "Selection Modes"
---

`input_map()` turns SVG regions into a form input. The `mode` decides what a click
does and what value your server receives. Internally every mode keeps a count per
region (`{region_id: int}`); the mode only changes how clicks update it and how it is
returned.

The pictures below use a grid of hexagons: any SVG paths work, not only maps.

## Single: a visual radio button

```python
from shinymap import input_map

input_map("choice", outline, mode="single")      # or mode=Single()
```

::: {layout="[[45,55]]" layout-valign="center"}
![](../images/generated/mode-single.svg){fig-alt="Hexagon grid with one hexagon selected" width="100%"}

::: {}
Clicking a region selects it and clears the previous one. Clicking the selected
region again clears it.

`input.choice()` → `"r7"`, or `None` when nothing is selected.
:::
:::

## Multiple: visual checkboxes

```python
input_map("choices", outline, mode="multiple")   # or Multiple(max_selection=3)
```

::: {layout="[[45,55]]" layout-valign="center"}
![](../images/generated/mode-multiple.svg){fig-alt="Hexagon grid with four hexagons selected" width="100%"}

::: {}
Each click toggles one region. With `Multiple(max_selection=n)`, clicks that would
select more than `n` regions are ignored.

`input.choices()` → `["r1", "r8", "r12", "r16"]`
:::
:::

## Cycle: a fixed number of states

```python
from shinymap import aes
from shinymap.mode import Cycle

input_map(
    "status", outline,
    mode=Cycle(n=4, aes=aes.Indexed(fill_color=["#e2e8f0", "#86efac", "#fde047", "#f87171"])),
)
```

::: {layout="[[45,55]]" layout-valign="center"}
![](../images/generated/mode-cycle.svg){fig-alt="Hexagon grid colored in four states" width="100%"}

::: {}
Each click moves a region to the next state, `0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 0`. `aes.Indexed` gives
one color per state, which suits ratings, traffic lights or "not started / doing / done".

`input.status()` → `{"r0": 0, "r1": 3, "r2": 2, ...}`
:::
:::

## Count: click to increment

```python
from shinymap.mode import Count

palette = ["#e2e8f0", "#bfdbfe", "#93c5fd", "#60a5fa", "#3b82f6", "#1d4ed8"]  # counts 0..5+
input_map(
    "votes", outline,
    mode=Count(aes=aes.Indexed(fill_color=palette)),
)
```

::: {layout="[[45,55]]" layout-valign="center"}
![](../images/generated/mode-count.svg){fig-alt="Hexagon grid shaded darker where counts are higher" width="100%"}

::: {}
Each click adds one, without a cap. The color stops at the last entry of
`aes.Indexed`, so with six colors every count of 5 or more shares the darkest one.
`Count(max_count=k)` stops it earlier, at entry `k`.

`input.votes()` → `{"r6": 3, "r7": 5, ...}`
:::
:::

## Raw values

Pass `raw=True` to receive the underlying `dict[str, int]` in every mode, e.g. when you
want the same processing for single and multiple selection.

## Output maps

`output_map()` shows a map without collecting input. Use `mode=Display(clickable=True)`
when you still want to react to clicks: they arrive as `input.<id>_click`
(or the `input_id` you pass). See [Aesthetics](aesthetics.qmd) for coloring regions by
value.
